comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
BATCHING EVIDENCE — measured against the landed renderer (merged `cf5155e528`) over the committed 178-body corpus. This bears on this story's central mechanism, so recording it before any further plan iteration.

## Run-length distribution (what batching could ever save)
233 contiguous SAFE runs across 884 `_RENDER` units. **106 of 233 runs (46%) are a single unit.**
```
len  1: 106 runs      len  6:  11      len 11:   4
len  2:  15           len  7:  14      len 12:   4
len  3:  22           len  8:  10      len 13:   6
len  4:  13           len  9:   6      len 14:   3
len  5:  15           len 10:   3      len 15:   1
```
Theoretical best case: 233 spawns instead of 884 = **74% fewer**. That is the ceiling, only reachable if every run batches successfully.

## Two candidate designs, both prototyped and measured
**(A) Run-level fallback (what the plan currently specifies — lift the preservation check to the run).** A single bad fragment poisons the whole run, degrading every unit in it to raw Markdown: **63 of 178 bodies (35%) lose richness** versus the landed per-unit renderer. Unacceptable.

**(B) Verify-then-accept, per-unit fallback.** Batch the run; accept the batched wiki only if the preservation check passes; otherwise re-render that run through the LANDED per-unit path. Measured: **157/178 identical** to per-unit, but only **775 vs 884 spawns = 12% fewer** — far below the 74% ceiling, because a failed batch pays BOTH the batch call and the per-unit calls.

## The reviewer's semantic concern is CONFIRMED
Even under (B), **21 of 178 bodies still render differently** from the per-unit path when the batch verifies successfully. pandoc parses block boundaries relative to surrounding content, so concatenating units into one commonmark document is genuinely not equivalent to rendering them separately (setext-style headings, lazy continuation, and reference-style links are the usual culprits). Batching is therefore not a transparent optimization — it changes output.

## The question this raises
As specified, safe-run batching buys ~12% fewer spawns while changing output on ~12% of bodies. The hazard it was introduced to fix is the ~0.3s/field spawn tax (~20 min of wall time on a large serial reconcile). Options:
1. **Descope batching** from this story, keeping the timeout + process-group reaping + fallback + compliance work (which are independently valuable and uncontested), and let the spawn tax be addressed by the cutover story's change-gated `rich_sha` render gate — which already avoids rendering unchanged bodies entirely, and is a much larger win than 12%.
2. **Keep batching under design (B)** and accept that ~12% of bodies render differently from today's landed output, with an AC pinning that difference as intended.
3. **Investigate the 21 divergent bodies** to find a document-assembly rule (e.g. forcing a hard block separator) that restores equivalence, then re-measure.

This exceeds what should be decided unilaterally — the story's stated mechanism does not deliver its stated benefit — so it is going back to the operator/driver rather than being silently redesigned. Work on `disparaged-parodistic-shrew` continues meanwhile; it is unblocked and independent of this decision.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DECISION (operator): **descope safe-run batching from this story** — Option 1 of the three recorded in the previous comment. The plan and ACs have been updated accordingly.

Rationale, as recorded by the operator: the measurements show batching's real benefit is ~12% fewer pandoc spawns (the 74% ceiling is unreachable because 46% of runs are single-unit) while changing rendered output on ~12% of corpus bodies. That is a bad trade, and **output divergence is exactly the class of behaviour change to escalate rather than ship silently**. Option 2 would have pinned that divergence as intended, which is not wanted; Option 3 would spend investigation to, at best, restore equivalence for the same 12%.

**Kept (uncontested, all still in scope):** the caller-side wall-clock timeout, process-group reaping via `rebar._proc.reap_process_group`, the existing PER-UNIT fallback semantics, the `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s` config surface, the wheel pin + CI check, and the new repo-root `NOTICE` recording pandoc's GPL entry.

**The spawn tax is not being ignored** — it is properly addressed by the cutover story `[rebar:3388-96e8-e14e-4221]`'s change-gated `rich_sha` skip, which avoids rendering unchanged bodies at all. That is a far larger win than 12% for the same hazard.

A new AC was added to make the reduced scope falsifiable: rendered output must be **byte-identical to the landed renderer across the whole committed 178-body corpus**, proving this story changes robustness only, never rendering.

Follow-up idea ticket filed for the spawn-cost question, carrying the 21-divergent-bodies analysis as its starting point, linked `discovered_from` this story.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED (pending full-suite + push). Recording the review finding that shaped it and three things the local gates caught, because two of them are traps for anyone writing subprocess tests in this repo.

## The re-review's one blocking finding was RIGHT, and cheap to have missed
The reviewer blocked on the plan omitting how the Markdown reaches pandoc's stdin: the landed `_convert` passes `input=markdown` to `subprocess.run`, while the ACLI pattern the plan cites spawns with `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` (acli takes no stdin). An implementer mirroring ACLI verbatim would have fed pandoc an EMPTY document — every unit failing its preservation check and degrading to raw Markdown, while every process-lifetime test still passed. The plan now states `stdin=subprocess.PIPE` + `communicate(input=…, timeout=…)`, and the code has two tests on it: one pinning `stdin == PIPE` and `!= DEVNULL` plus the exact argv, and one "guards the guard" test proving `_convert("")` differs from `_convert(unit)` — otherwise the first test would pass under the broken implementation too. Re-review after the edit: **PASS, 0 blocking, 6 advisory.**

## TRAP 1: do not monkeypatch `subprocess.Popen` in this repo's tests
My first version patched the module attribute to inject a fake pandoc. The test passed and then HUNG in teardown, surfacing as a 100s pytest-timeout inside `selectors.poll(None)` — which reads like infrastructure, not like a test bug. Cause: the autouse `_no_repo_commits` fixture in `tests/conftest.py` shells out to git during teardown via `tests/_isolation.py`, and `monkeypatch` had not yet undone the patch, so **the conftest's git call spawned my fake instead**, then blocked on its pipes forever.

The fix is better than the workaround: hand `_convert` a path to a REAL executable stand-in (a chmod +x script) instead of patching the spawn. Everything stays real — argv, pipes, timeout, reap — and nothing else in the process is affected. Anyone testing a subprocess seam here should do the same.

## TRAP 2: the stand-in's grandchild holds the pipes, so never hand its pid back on stderr
The whole point of the stand-in is a grandchild that INHERITS the pipes and spins. A test that reads the pid off `proc.stderr` waits for EOF, and EOF needs every holder gone — so if the reap ever regresses, the test DEADLOCKS instead of failing. The pid now comes back through a file.

## TRAP 3: `check_wall_clock_asserts` wants its marker on the line DIRECTLY above
`assert elapsed < 60` is a legitimate hang-guard (it separates "the 1s timeout fired" from "we waited out the stand-in's 300s sleep" — the only two ways `_convert` can return there). The gate accepts `# timing: hang-guard — <reason>` only within one line of the assert; a marker at the top of a multi-line comment block is NOT seen.

## Corpus byte-identity: FULL, not sampled
I initially strided the equivalence comparison, believing the full corpus would cost ~9 minutes. That estimate was wrong — it was measuring the Popen-patching hang, not the work. Measured properly: **~880 renderable units rendered twice (new path + a transcript of the pre-hardening one), all byte-identical, in 89s** — the same order as the existing corpus suite. So the AC is met literally, over the whole committed 178-body corpus, with no sampling.

## Delivered
`wiki_render.py` (own `Popen` + `start_new_session=True` + caller-side `communicate(input=…, timeout=…)` + `_reap_pandoc` over `rebar._proc.reap_process_group`, per-unit fallback unchanged); `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s` across the four-file config surface (schema + validator, auto-derived `REBAR_RECONCILER_DC_PANDOC_TIMEOUT_S`, regenerated `tests/golden/config_surface.json`, `docs/config.md`); a NEW repo-root `NOTICE` recording pandoc 3.6.1 / GPL-2.0-or-later / upstream and how it reaches an install; a CI `pandoc pin + NOTICE provenance` gate that fails on a loosened pin, a multi-version pin, a missing NOTICE, or a NOTICE that no longer names the pinned wheel or its licence. 14 new tests; `make lint`, `make typecheck`, complexity baseline (active=53 new=0 increased=0), and the `check_*` gates all clean.

Note the wheel was ALREADY pinned `pypandoc-binary==1.15` by `repressive-delectable-swan` in two places, so this story adds the VERIFICATION rather than the pin.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
LANDED — Gerrit **1724** MERGED (`a147945aae`), `LLM-Review +1` + `Verified +1` first time.

## A follow-up change (1729) because ONE AC named a test I had replaced with a CI gate
Auditing the ACs against merged main rather than against my own memory of the work: the last AC names `tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py` explicitly, and I had implemented that check as a CI workflow step instead. The CI gate is genuinely useful — it fails on a loosened pin, a multi-version pin, a missing NOTICE, or a NOTICE that no longer names the pinned wheel or its licence — but it is CI-ONLY, so the first signal of drift is a `Verified -1` after a push, and the reasoning lives in shell rather than beside the assertions.

1729 adds the named test. It deliberately does NOT check the version twice independently: `pyproject.toml` and `NOTICE` are asserted to AGREE, because the interesting failure here is not a missing NOTICE (loud, obvious) but a pin bump that quietly leaves the record describing a binary nobody distributes any more. Two independent version checks would both pass in exactly that case. It also asserts the pin is a single `==` rather than a range (an unknowable version cannot be recorded at all) and that NOTICE says pandoc arrives only via the optional `wiki` extra (without which the record would overstate the obligation for installs shipping no pandoc).

## AC test-name drift, recorded so the ticket matches reality
The other six ACs are all satisfied, but four named tests that do not exist under those names — the plan was written before the tests were. The description has been updated to the real names rather than left citing fictions:
- `test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back` → the timeout half is `test_the_timeout_default_matches_the_config_default` / `test_the_timeout_is_read_from_config` / `test_a_non_positive_timeout_falls_back_rather_than_disabling_rendering`; the REAP half is `test_a_timeout_reaps_the_whole_process_group_not_just_the_child` + `test_the_child_leads_its_own_process_group`.
- `test_dc_pandoc_error_degrades` → `test_a_timed_out_unit_degrades_to_its_original_markdown`, `test_a_nonzero_exit_degrades_without_raising`, `test_an_unspawnable_pandoc_degrades_without_raising`.
- `test_dc_hardening_does_not_change_output` → `test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer`.

Splitting each into its separate property was the right call — `test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back` as written would have had to assert the timeout, the group reap AND the fallback in one body, and the group-reap assertion is the one that must not be diluted.

All 7 ACs are now ticked. Remaining before close: 1729 green and submitted.

compiled_state.description:
# DC renderer robustness & compliance hardening

## Context / Problem
The DC path shells out to pandoc per field. Two hazards from the DC experiment remain
in scope: (1) **pathological-input hang** — one corpus body spun pandoc's jira reader
13.5 min at 95.8% CPU, and pypandoc sets no timeout, so a single field can stall the
reconcile indefinitely; (2) **licence provenance** — pandoc is GPL and rides inside the
`pypandoc-binary` wheel, so its pin and licence must be recorded.

A third hazard, the ~0.3s/field subprocess spawn tax (~20 min of wall time on a large
serial reconcile), was originally to be addressed here by batching contiguous safe
units into one pandoc call. **That is now DESCOPED** — see "Descoped" below.

## Prior art / dependency boundaries (do NOT re-decide 271c's choices)
- **The renderer and its pandoc delivery are owned by 271c.** Story
  `[rebar:271c-e88f-3220-4c9b]` LANDED the pure renderer at
  `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` (merged `cf5155e528`), with pandoc from the pinned
  **`pypandoc-binary==1.15` wheel** (bundled binary, **pandoc 3.6.1**) via a `wiki` extra. This
  story hardens THAT module and VERIFIES that pin; it adds no system pandoc.
- Live wiring of `WikiTextCodec` belongs to the cutover story
  `[rebar:3388-96e8-e14e-4221]` and is out of scope here, as is the change-gated
  "no-op → no pandoc spawn" property (that story's `rich_sha` gate).

## Approach
- **Hard timeout + process-group reaping.** A plain `subprocess.run(timeout=)` reaps only
  the DIRECT child, so a jira-reader spinning at ~95.8% CPU (a pipe-holding grandchild)
  survives (bug d843, bpo-30154). So the renderer MUST NOT use pypandoc's high-level
  `convert_text`/`convert_file` API (no process handle): it locates pandoc via
  `pypandoc.get_pandoc_path()`, builds its OWN
  `subprocess.Popen([pandoc_path, …], start_new_session=True)` with
  `stdin=subprocess.PIPE` and delivers the unit via
  `proc.communicate(input=<unit markdown>, timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s)` — matching the
  landed `_convert`'s `input=markdown` semantics, NOT the cited ACLI case's
  `stdin=DEVNULL` (acli takes no stdin; pandoc READS the unit from stdin, so copying
  that kwarg verbatim would feed pandoc empty input and degrade every unit) — and, on
  `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, passes that `Popen` to **`rebar._proc.reap_process_group`**
  (`_proc.py:26`) — `killpg` SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL→bounded drain, already reused by the
  ACLI transport and grounding harness — killing the whole group. It kills/drains only
  AFTER a timeout is detected, so caller-side detection is required
  (`acli_subprocess.py`'s pattern). This REPLACES the landed `subprocess.run(timeout=30)`
  in `_convert` (`wiki_render.py`), which reaps only the direct child.
- **The timeout is a config key** (`reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default **10s**):
  >30× the observed ~0.3s/field render and ~80× below the 13.5-min hang;
  `grace`/`drain` reuse the ACLI caller's constants.
- **Fallback granularity is UNCHANGED — per unit.** On timeout or non-zero exit the unit
  degrades to its original Markdown verbatim (echo-safe), exactly as the landed
  `_render_unit` already does on conversion or preservation failure. One unit's failure
  never affects another, and no rendered output changes.
- **Compliance:** pin the wheel, create a repo-root `NOTICE` recording pandoc's GPL
  entry, and verify the pin in CI.

## Descoped: safe-run batching (operator decision, evidence-backed)
Batching contiguous safe units into one pandoc call was prototyped and measured against the
landed renderer over the committed 178-body corpus, and is **removed from this story**: the
ceiling is 233 runs vs 884 units, but 106 of 233 runs (46%) are single-unit so it is
unreachable; run-level fallback costs 63/178 bodies (35%) their richness; verify-then-accept
keeps richness but yields only 12% fewer spawns; and **21/178 bodies still render DIFFERENTLY
even when a batch verifies**, because pandoc parses block boundaries relative to surrounding
content. ~12% fewer spawns for changed output on ~12% of bodies is a bad trade, and a silent
rendering change is not something to ship. Full measurements are in this ticket's comments; a
follow-up idea ticket carries the 21-divergent-bodies analysis if spawn cost matters later.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` — replace `_convert`'s `subprocess.run` with an
  own `subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True)` over `pypandoc.get_pandoc_path()`, the
  caller-side timeout, and `rebar._proc.reap_process_group`. Per-unit fallback behaviour
  and all rendered output stay byte-identical.
- `pyproject.toml` — pin the `pypandoc-binary` wheel version (extends 271c's pin).
- config (`reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default 10s) across the standard four-file
  `reconciler.*` surface: `_config_schema.py` (field + `_as_float(v, k, minimum=0.0)`
  validator), `_config_sources.py` (auto-derived `REBAR_RECONCILER_DC_PANDOC_TIMEOUT_S`),
  `tests/golden/config_surface.json` (deliberately REGENERATED — the guard is removal-only, so
  it will NOT flag a new key's omission), and `docs/config.md`.
- CI workflow — verify the wheel pin (NOT an acli-style sha check).
- **`NOTICE` (NEW file, repo root)** — the repo has only `LICENSE` today and no
  SBOM/notice artifact, so this story CREATES `NOTICE` and records the wheel-bundled
  pandoc's GPL entry (name, version 3.6.1, licence, upstream) there.
- `tests/` — timeout, reaping and fallback tests over the vendored DC corpus.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every pandoc invocation runs under a caller-side wall-clock timeout via
  `proc.communicate(timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s)` (config `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`,
  default 10s — above the ~0.3s render, below the 13.5-min hang); verified in
  `test_wiki_render_hardening.py` by `test_the_timeout_default_matches_the_config_default`,
  `test_the_timeout_is_read_from_config` and
  `test_a_non_positive_timeout_falls_back_rather_than_disabling_rendering`.
- [x] On `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` the whole process GROUP is reaped via
  `rebar._proc.reap_process_group`, so a CPU-spinning grandchild is killed rather than
  orphaned; verified by `test_a_timeout_reaps_the_whole_process_group_not_just_the_child`
  (a real stand-in executable forks a spinning grandchild; the assertion is on the
  GRANDCHILD) plus `test_the_child_leads_its_own_process_group`.
- [x] On timeout or non-zero exit the affected UNIT degrades to its original Markdown
  without raising and the render returns; verified by
  `test_a_timed_out_unit_degrades_to_its_original_markdown`,
  `test_a_nonzero_exit_degrades_without_raising` and
  `test_an_unspawnable_pandoc_degrades_without_raising`.
- [x] Rendered output is byte-identical to the landed renderer for the whole committed
  178-body corpus, proving this story changes robustness only, not rendering; verified by
  `test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer` (~880 units, each rendered
  through both the new path and a transcript of the pre-hardening one).
- [x] `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s` is reachable from config file and environment and
  documented; verified by `test_the_timeout_is_read_from_config`,
  `test_the_timeout_is_reachable_from_the_environment`, the regenerated
  `tests/golden/config_surface.json`, and the `docs/config.md` entry.
- [x] The pandoc binary comes from the `pypandoc-binary` wheel pinned by version in
  `pyproject.toml` (pinned `==1.15` by `271c`) and the pin is verified in CI; verified by the
  new `pandoc pin + NOTICE provenance gate` CI step plus
  `test_the_wheel_is_pinned_to_exactly_one_version`.
- [x] The wheel-bundled pandoc's GPL licence is recorded in a NEW repo-root `NOTICE` file
  (only `LICENSE` existed), naming pandoc, version 3.6.1 and its licence; verified by
  `tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py`, which also binds NOTICE to the pyproject pin
  so the two cannot drift apart.
